Activity 3.7 — Test for fat
You will need: the same food samples; plain paper.
Take a small piece of each food from Activity 3.6.
Place each on a separate piece of paper. Label the papers.
Fold the paper over the food and press firmly. Do not tear it.
If a food is watery, set the paper aside until it dries — a wet patch is
not an oily patch, and confusing the two will ruin your result.
Hold each paper up to the light.
shows that the food contains fat.
An oily patch that light passes through
Record your observations in Table 3.3.
ACTIVITY
Activity 3.8 — Test for protein
Your teacher will demonstrate this activity. Read the precautions before
anything else.
You will need: the same food samples; pestle and mortar; clean test tubes;
two droppers; copper sulfate solution; caustic soda solution.
Grind each food sample into a paste or powder with the pestle and mortar.
Put about half a teaspoon of each into a separate clean test tube.
Add two or three teaspoons of water to each tube and shake well.
Using one dropper, add two drops of copper sulfate solution to each tube.
Using a different dropper, add ten drops of caustic soda solution to each tube.
Shake, then leave the tubes undisturbed for a few minutes.
A violet colour indicates the presence of protein.
Record your observations in Table 3.3.
— read before you start
PRECAUTIONS
• Copper sulfate and caustic soda are harmful chemicals. Do not touch them
unless your teacher tells you to.
If any chemical touches your skin, wash the area with plenty of water at once
and tell your teacher.
• Never put these chemicals in your mouth. Do not try to smell them.
Use a separate dropper for each chemical. Never return unused chemical to its bottle.
Wash your hands when you have finished.
